headline: Approved amended minutes of the previous meeting; discussed Swarthmore Street tree safety, arborist assessments, and grant work.
summary: Residents of Swarthmore Street asked that street trees be evaluated after a large oak fell. The Commission discussed hiring a qualified arborist, building a tree inventory, and grant plans. The Commission approved amended minutes 5-0.
decisions: Approved the July 21, 2026 minutes with spelling corrections, by a 5-0 roll call vote.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
Tree Commission Minutes  
Regular Meeting 
5:30 PM, August 18, 2026 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2nd Floor Conference 
Room 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075
Click to View Agenda 
1. CALL TO ORDER  
The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner Dr. M. Montgomery at 5:36 PM.
2. ATTENDANCE  
The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were present:
Commissioner Dr. Michael Montgomery, Chair
Commissioner Susan L. Neitlich
Commissioner Diane E. Hoffman
Commissioner Dr. Nathan Havill
Commissioner Kyle Dougherty
Also in attendance were Briana J. Belton-Robinson, Boards and Commissions Clerk, and
about 6 members of the public who joined in person, all residents of Swarthmore Street.
Roll Call Summary: Present, Voting: 5; Present, Not Voting: 0; Absent: 0; Excused: 0.
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
Regular Meeting of July 21, 2026
Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Tuesday, July
21st, 2026, with amendments.
Please see the corrections approved for amendment:
Commissioner S. Neitlich requested that the July 21st, 2026 minutes be amended; typo
and spelling corrections were identified.
• Corrected the spelling of 'Alenier Street'
• Corrected the spelling of 'ConnCORP'
• Corrected the spelling of Commissioner K. 'Dougherty'
The motion to amend the previous agenda was made by Commissioner D. Hoffman and 
seconded by Commissioner Dr. N. Havill. 
Vote by Roll Call: 
Yes 
Commissioner Dr. M. Montgomery 
Commissioner S. Neitlich  
Amended 09/18/2026
Commissioner K. Dougherty 
Commissioner Dr. N. Havill 
Commissioner D. Hoffman 
 
The motion passed. 
Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 5, No 0, Abstentions, Absent 0. 
  
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 Several residents of Swarthmore Street addressed the Commission regarding the condition 
and safety of mature trees along the street. Residents emphasized that they value the 
established tree canopy and were not advocating for wholesale tree removal, but 
requested professional assessment, appropriate pruning, removal of hazardous trees 
where necessary, and replacement planting. 
 
Raquel Betts, Swarthmore Street, expressed concern about the condition of the trees and 
requested that they be evaluated to determine their current health and potential safety 
risks. 
 
Dr. Jennifer McCarthy, 51 Swarthmore Street, reported that a large, mature oak tree 
recently fell between her residence and the neighboring property at 57 Swarthmore Street, 
causing property damage. Dr. McCarthy stated that the tree was approximately 125 years 
old, based on its rings. She described the incident as a “near miss,” noting the potential for 
serious injury or loss of life had the tree fallen differently or had anyone been outside at the 
time. She commended the Town for its rapid and professional emergency response and 
requested that the remaining street trees be evaluated. 
 
Carol Woven, 56 Swarthmore Street, described a 2019 incident in which a large tree limb 
fell onto and totaled her vehicle. She expressed concern about both falling trees and large 
limbs and stated that she had previously requested an evaluation of the street trees. She 
also commended the Town’s response to the recent fallen tree but emphasized the need 
for preventive attention to the remaining trees. 
 
Michael Milazzo, 70 Swarthmore Street, stated that the mature trees were one of the 
reasons he chose to live on Swarthmore Street. While supporting an evaluation of the trees 
and appropriate action to address safety concerns, he emphasized that he did not want all 
of the trees removed. He noted that some residents have privately retained arborists to 
address tree concerns. 
 
Amanda Levitt, 30 Swarthmore Street, emphasized the environmental benefits of the tree 
canopy, including shade, temperature regulation, and stormwater absorption on a street 
that experiences flooding. She supported having a qualified arborist evaluate the trees' 
health, root systems, and branch structure. She suggested pruning healthy trees, removing 
trees determined to pose significant risks, and replanting where removals are necessary. 
 
Mimsie Coleman, 57 Swarthmore Street, presented photographs and video documenting 
the recently fallen oak tree, its root system, and conditions along Swarthmore Street. She 
expressed concern that the narrow planting area between the sidewalk and roadway has 
limited the large trees' ability to develop adequate root systems. She stated that the 
exposed roots of the fallen tree appeared delicate and deteriorated and expressed concern
that similar conditions may exist among other mature trees on the street. She also 
discussed leaning trees and sidewalk damage associated with the root systems. Ms. 
Coleman stated that she had spoken with Chris Rhone regarding possible sidewalk repair 
options, in consultation with the Town Engineer, and had requested a professional 
assessment of the remaining trees and their root systems. The photographs and video 
were provided to the Commission for the record. Ms. Coleman submitted videos and 
photos (see the agenda packet) for the public record of trees: 
 
• Video #1 
• Video #2 
 
Cristina and Giuseppe Moscarini, 35 Swarthmore Street, submitted comments that were 
shared with the Commission in their absence. 
 
Following public comment, Chair Dr. M. Montgomery stated that the Town and 
Commission are exploring the retention of a qualified arborist with Tree Risk Assessment 
Qualification (TRAQ) credentials. The Commission is particularly interested in an arborist 
with the ability to conduct advanced assessment of the base and internal condition of trees. 
Potential approaches discussed included crown thinning, cabling where appropriate, and 
further assessment before determining whether individual trees require removal. 
 
Chairman Dr. Montgomery stated that the Town has begun reviewing conditions on 
Swarthmore Street and intends to incorporate the trees into the Town’s inventory and GIS 
database. He also discussed proactive replacement planting and the need to balance tree 
preservation, public safety, sidewalk conditions, utilities, and long-term canopy 
management. 
 
Chairman Dr. Montgomery announced that he would be joining the Town as a part-time 
employee to assist with management of the Trees for Communities Grant and related 
work. 
 
In response to a question regarding whether residents may hire a private arborist to 
perform work on a Town tree, Chairman Dr. Montgomery stated that private work may be 
permitted with authorization from the Tree Warden. The proposed work and contractor 
must be identified, and a permit obtained before work is done. He encouraged residents to 
first determine what work is necessary through an assessment by a qualified professional. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE   
 The Commission reviewed correspondence submitted by residents to the Commission’s 
official email account, HBC_Trees@Hamden.com. 
 
Roxanne Kohilakis, 34 Humiston Avenue, contacted the Commission regarding a tree that 
had been removed approximately two years earlier. She stated that the tree was expected 
to be replaced, and that grass seed was to be applied, but the work had not yet been 
completed. She also reported concerns regarding bees in the remaining stump. 
 
Bowen Dou, corner of Middle Road and Glen Parkway, requested evaluation of three Town 
trees due to falling debris, unexpected limb or tree failure, potential safety concerns,
property risks, and reported damage in the surrounding area. 
 
Josie Jayworth, 43 Quentin Street, requested an update regarding a previously submitted 
request for a new tree. Chairman Dr. Montgomery reported that the resident had since 
been contacted and the location had been marked to receive a tree. 
 
Jennifer Cherrington, 199 Grandview Avenue, expressed concern about a large, mature 
tree that appeared to be deteriorating and dropping limbs onto the sidewalk. She noted 
concern for pedestrians, including children and residents walking dogs, and submitted 
photographs for review. Please see photos in the agenda packet. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No executive session was held. 
7. REPORTS   
 
 
  1. Tree Warden Report  
  No Tree Warden Report was presented. 
  2. Plant Sciences Days, Lockwood Farm  
  The Commission discussed its participation in Plant Sciences Day at Lockwood Farm. 
Members reviewed outreach opportunities, educational materials, public engagement, 
and potential follow-up from conversations held during the event. 
 
The Commission also discussed whether certain outreach and educational expenses 
could appropriately be supported through the Trees for Communities Grant. 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Whitneyville Library Shrub and Tree Renovation  
  The Commission discussed the Whitneyville Library shrub and tree renovation project 
and upcoming activities associated with the site. Discussion included tree and shrub 
planting, community participation, and coordination of future work. 
  2. Trees for Communities Grant (Fall Plans, Webpage)  
  The Commission discussed the Trees for Communities Grant, including upcoming fall 
activities, project management, outreach, and proposed updates to the Commission’s 
webpage. 
 
Chairman Dr. Montgomery stated that an updated work plan was due to the 
Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) by August 
30, 2026. He explained that proposed changes included moving project-management 
responsibilities from a contractual arrangement to a part-time Town position. 
 
Chairman Dr. Montgomery stated that he would serve in the part-time position and 
assist with administration and coordination of the grant.
The Commission also discussed improving the visibility of grant-related programs and 
other Tree Commission activities through the Town website, social media, press 
releases, and other communications. 
  3. Friends of the Library Audio-Podcast: Participation  
  The Commission discussed participation in the Friends of the Library audio/podcast 
initiative and representation of tree-related topics. 
 
Commissioner D. Hoffman will represent the Hamden Alliance for Trees, while 
Commissioners S. Neitlich and K. Dougherty will represent the Hamden Tree 
Commission. The discussion will focus broadly on trees and related community 
issues. Chairman Dr. Montgomery stated that he would provide additional talking 
points if needed. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Tree Inventory  
  Chairman Dr. M. Montgomery reported that he had spoken with Andrew Kinlock, GIS 
Coordinator, Engineering Department, regarding the Town’s tree inventory. Mr. 
Kinlock has been developing the Town’s GIS-based tree database and has completed 
survey work related to the inventory. 
 
The Commission discussed the importance of field verification, or “ground truthing,” to 
supplement GIS and aerial information. The inventory is intended to provide accurate 
information regarding tree locations and characteristics and support future tree 
management, planting, maintenance, and grant-related activities. 
 
  
  2. Sustainable CT Tree Survey  
  The Commission discussed the Sustainable CT Tree Survey and the potential value 
of participating. Members discussed coordination with Sustainable CT and related 
organizations, the information required for the survey, and how the process could help 
identify and document the Town’s existing tree-management practices. 
10. ANNOUCEMENTS   
 Additional discussion was held regarding upcoming Commission activities, community 
outreach, tree planting, grant implementation, and coordination with Town departments. 
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 Chairman M. Montgomery requested a motion to adjourn the meeting. 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The meeting adjourned at approximately 7:45 P.M.
